title: Compact Request Inspector — Threadline & Correlation Lens
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As traffic patterns diversify across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments, engineers need a compact, fast inspector to debug single requests without leaving the main dashboard. This ticket designs a compact request inspector (inline drawer) focused on: (1) a condensed threadline timeline that surfaces span boundaries and latency hotspots, (2) a correlation lens that highlights related spans across services by correlation ID and by causal edges, and (3) quick filters and actions for common debug flows. The inspector must be readable at small widths, render large traces fast (virtualized lane rendering), and provide progressive disclosure for span details to avoid noise.

Scope: Deliver high-fidelity prototype, interaction spec, accessibility notes, and a handoff-ready assets package for engineering + QA. Not in scope: backend sampling changes, long-term storage UX, or tracing ingestion pipeline changes.
acceptance_criteria: Compact inspector opens as inline drawer from dashboard or request row and preserves scroll context
Threadline shows span start/end as compressed lanes with sparkline density and highlights top 3 latency contributors
Correlation Lens can filter by correlation ID and visually link matching spans across lanes, with copy-to-clipboard and jump-to-trace actions
Inspector renders 2000 spans in under 300ms on a representative dev machine via virtualization and incremental paint
Prototype includes keyboard navigation (open, close, expand span, jump to next/prev correlation) and ARIA labels for screen readers
decisions: Inline drawer chosen over full-page modal to keep context with dashboard filters
Use compressed lane rendering (one pixel per X ms zoom) to fit long traces without horizontal scroll by default
Correlation Lens implements visual linking (curved bezier overlays) only in expanded view to avoid visual clutter in compact mode
Expose copy/jump actions on hover for each correlation match to minimize accidental navigation
tradeoffs: Progressive disclosure reduces cognitive load but increases clicks to get full span stack and logs
Rendering 2000+ spans requires virtualization; initial paint will omit deep metadata until expanded which slightly delays per-span log visibility
Bezier overlay linking is visually helpful but may be expensive with extreme cardinality — limited to top N matches by default
tasks: Finalize Figma frames for v3 and export component tokens (Evelyn)
Create interaction spec (keyboard/ARIA/state transitions) and handoff doc (Aisha)
Implement virtualization strategy doc and example harness for 2k spans (eng pairing: Marcus + Javier)
Add unit tests for copy/jump actions and correlation filter (QA)
Performance review with infra team to validate 300ms render target on representative hardware
open_questions: Should correlation lens support multi-value correlation (trace_id + custom_correlation_id) or only the latter?
What is the expected canonical payload for span tags we rely on for quick attribution (service.version, kernel, gpu_id)?
Do we allow persistent pinning of an inspected request so it remains open when changing dashboard filters?
How should we surface sampled vs unsampled traces when correlation references missing spans?

accessibility_notes: All interactive span chips must have ARIA labels with span name, duration, and index for screen readers
Keyboard focus order must follow list order: open drawer -> timeline -> span list -> correlation filters -> actions
Heatstrip colors meet AA contrast after suggested tweak; provide a high-contrast toggle in user settings
Allow screen-reader users to opt into a 'list view' textual fallback that enumerates spans and key tags
performance_constraints: Target initial meaningful paint for inspector under 300ms for traces up to 2k spans on a standard dev VM
Virtualize lanes and lazy-load span metadata and linked logs
Limit curvature overlay to top 50 correlation matches by default; allow override in advanced settings
Prefer canvas or WebGL for rendering overlays when overlay count > 200 to avoid DOM thrash
